build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not map data: the unpacker runs on past the 1024-byte tile layer until its input count runs out, decoding the next entry's packed bytes with this entry's table; nothing reads them and the map is never written back from here
extra: map 31: its tile layer, one byte a square, 32 rows of 32, unpacked from T35/L13 by enter_map ($25BD)

comments.text: Class layer, rows 0-31 of 32x32: a nibble a square, even column in the high nibble (map_class_at $0953). Squares by class: 0: 62, 1: 152, 2: 13, 3: 1, 9: 1, 10: 9, 11: 785, 12: 1.
Number layer, rows 0-31: one byte a square, the entry of its class's list that holds the square's record (map_number_row $098E, action_record $09B8).

The number of square (9, 29). Game `$B4F0` `bit $39A9` names it because of the BIT-skip idiom: the operand's bytes are the `lda #$39` the code enters at `$B4F1`. On choose_attack's path through the LDA #$50 at $B4EE (api_is_ranged_class at $B4E4 returning carry clear and weapon_rounds at $B4E9 returning 0) the BIT does execute and read this byte, but its flags are replaced before anything tests them (N and Z by LDA #$92 at $1DC4, V by the ADC at $28E5, both on game_msg's path), so its value never matters.
